'''Samuel Clement Bradford''' (10 January 1878 in London – 13 November 1948)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pledge |first=H. T. |date=1948 |title=Dr. S. C. Bradford |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=162 |issue=4128 |pages=917–918 |doi=10.1038/162917b0 |issn=1476-4687|doi-access=free |bibcode=1948Natur.162..917P }}</ref> was a British mathematician, [[librarian]] and [[documentalist]] at the [[Science Museum (London)|Science Museum]] in London. He developed "[[Bradford's law]]" (or the "law of scattering") regarding differences in demand for scientific journals.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1985 |title=Sources of information on specific subjects 1934 |url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/016555158501000407 |journal=Journal of Information Science |language=en |volume=10 |issue=4 |pages=176–180 |doi=10.1177/016555158501000407 |s2cid=220492544 |issn=0165-5515|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brookes |first=B. C. |date=1969 |title=Bradford's Law and the Bibliography of Science |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/224953a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=224 |issue=5223 |pages=953–956 |doi=10.1038/224953a0 |pmid=4902657 |bibcode=1969Natur.224..953B |s2cid=4186617 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This work influences [[bibliometrics]] and [[citation analysis]] of scientific publications. Bradford founded the British Society for International Bibliography (BSIB) (est. 1927) and he was elected president of [[International Federation for Information and Documentation]] (FID) in 1945. Bradford was a strong proponent of [[Universal Decimal Classification]] and of establishing [[Abstract (summary)|abstract]]s of the [[scientific literature]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=BRADFORD |first=S.C. |date=1977 |title=Recollections of a colleague whose memory may be at fault |url=https://doi.org/10.1108/eb026640 |journal=Journal of Documentation |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=173–179 |doi=10.1108/eb026640 |issn=0022-0418|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He became head of the [[Science Museum Library|Science Library]] in 1925 and became Keeper of the Science Library in 1930.<ref name="GI S. C. Bradford">{{cite web |title=Dr S C Bradford, Science Museum Librarian, 1900. |url=https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/detail/news-photo/in-1898-bradford-started-work-at-the-science-museum-as-a-news-photo/90733793 |website=Getty Images |publisher=Getty Images. |access-date=26 November 2025 |language=en-gb |date=14 September 2009}}</ref> He was succeeded in this role by [[Ernest Lancaster-Jones]] in 1935.<ref name="Wyatt (2010) Science Museum’s Library">{{cite journal |last1=Wyatt |first1=Nicholas |editor1-last=Morris |editor1-first=Peter J. T. |title=Waves of Change: How the Science Museum's Library Rose, Fell and Rose Again |journal=Science for the Nation: Perspectives on the History of the Science Museum |date=2010 |pages=136–156 |doi=10.1057/9780230283145_7 |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1057/9780230283145_7 |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan UK |location=London |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
